about: The authoritative list of OpenLogo's built-in names for this specification version: every keyword and every primitive, aliases included. spec/grammar.md:363 governs them with one rule -- a program may not DECLARE a built-in name, and may BIND a value to any name -- and spec/grammar.md:414 versions them with the specification. This file is that list in machine-readable form, and CI asserts the implementation's registries equal it exactly, in both directions (docs/adr/0021-built-in-names-list-and-ci-gate.md). It is normative and maintainer-owned like the rest of spec/. Membership here answers one question only -- may a program declare this name? -- and never how a word is highlighted, which spec/tooling.md owns as an independent axis. Each registry's `note` is NON-NORMATIVE rationale: it records why a tag is shaped as it is, and nothing verifies its content beyond the mechanical checks the gate applies -- no control characters, no accessor value, and no counting word. A note must never restate data this file already carries, because a restatement is a second list and a second list is the one thing this file exists to remove. This narrow rule applies to `note` only: `invariants`, `profiles.about`, `tokenClassKeyword` and every `excluded[].rationale` are normative or required as data by ADR-0021 and are not demoted by it.

invariants.unconditional: Every profile's keywords and primitives are built-in names in EVERY implementation, whether or not that profile is claimed (spec/grammar.md:408). `profile` below is metadata for docs and tooling; nothing may branch on it when deciding whether a name is blocked at a declaration slot.
invariants.precedence: A name reachable from two registries is filed ONCE. Precedence is TWO-LEVEL and the order matters: first by CATEGORY, `keyword` beating `primitive` regardless of where the tags sit -- which is what files `thing` as a keyword though `core-primitive` also holds it; then, among registries of the SAME category, by the key order of `registries` below -- which is what files `to` under core-language rather than heritage, since `reserved` precedes `heritage-form-head`. Reordering `registries` therefore never changes a keyword/primitive verdict, only which same-category tag supplies the `profile`. Its `profile` follows the precedence-winning registry. The full membership is always recorded in `registries` on the entry, never inferred from `category` or `profile`, so losing one of two registrations fails the gate instead of matching a summary that still looks right.
invariants.bothDirections: The gate compares structured entries, not a flat name set: every name here must be in the implementation and every name in the implementation must be here, with `category`, `profile` and `registries` all checked. Each registry names TWO accessors because the two directions need different shapes -- a `lookup` (is this name here?) and an `enumerate` (what does this hold?). The *PrimitiveArity functions are lookups only, so their tags enumerate through `profilePrimitiveNames` instead. Those two views derive from ONE table, so they cannot disagree about membership; what the gate's agreement check really catches there is case-normalisation mismatch, because the lookup lowercases its argument and the enumerator does not.
invariants.accessorStatus: `present` means the accessor MUST resolve as a public export of @openlogo/parser; a missing one is drift. `declared` means decided but not yet created: the gate accepts its absence and FAILS if it ever resolves, because at that moment it should have become `present`. Status attaches per accessor, not per tag, because a tag can be split. At 0.1.0 every accessor is `present`.
invariants.derivedEnumeration: The nine profile-keyed primitive tags enumerate through ONE accessor, `profilePrimitiveNames`, called with the tag's own profile. Nine hand-written per-profile enumerators would each be a claim about a registry, maintained by hand, beside the registry -- the shape this whole file exists to remove. The derived form also lets the gate sweep OL_CHECK_PROFILES directly, so a TENTH profile that gains a primitive table is covered with no edit to this file at all.

reserved.note: ADR-0021 named this table before issue #837 renamed the vocabulary from reserved words to keywords. The tag name is ADR-0021's closed vocabulary and deliberately does not track the accessor it points at, so a further rename moves the accessor and leaves the tag alone.

profile-reserved.note: The same ADR-0021 rename applies here. Keyed by profile rather than flat, because each word belongs to a different profile: it therefore supplies each entry's profile directly and declares none of its own at tag level.

core-primitive.note: Why the two roles cannot disagree about membership: both read the same table. What differs between them is case normalisation, which is what the agreement check actually catches.

turtle-primitive.note: Why the one-word spellings are not ordinary members here: each is a separate arity entry bound to a canonical, and that edge is carried by this tag's alias accessors rather than by its lookup and enumerate pair.

data-primitive.note: No exception worth recording. The tag exists so that this profile's table is compared like every other, rather than being known only to the implementation.

educational-primitive.note: Why this table needs no exception: the AI coaching command has a registry of its own rather than being carved out of this one.

geometry-primitive.note: Why this table is far smaller than its profile: the derived standard library is OpenLogo source, listed under `excluded` and never here.

interaction-primitive.note: Why this table holds fewer names than its profile does: the profile's words are keywords, held by the profile-keyed keyword registry, and only callable primitives are filed here.

sound-primitive.note: No exception worth recording. The tag exists so that this profile's table is compared like every other, rather than being known only to the implementation.

sprites-primitive.note: Why this table holds fewer names than its profile does: the profile's words are keywords, held by the profile-keyed keyword registry, and only callable primitives are filed here.

tutor-primitive.note: ADR-0021 recorded both of this tag's accessors as `declared` -- decided but not yet created -- and named issue #841 as the slice that would create them. The tree reached them by a better route (issues #838 and #874): one derived accessor over the whole profile-keyed registry, rather than a hand-written enumerator per profile. The ADR is a dated record of the decision, not of the code.

heritage-alias.note: Why `category` cannot be derived from arity-table membership here: the short spellings are in no primitive arity table at all, only their canonicals are, so they are registered solely under this tag.

heritage-form-head.note: Why these carry no `aliasOf`: they are grammar form heads, not name-for-name substitutions. They are keywords elsewhere too, so they lose precedence on the same-category key order rather than on category.

heritage-worded-form-head.note: Why this carries no `aliasOf`: a worded form is a grammar spelling, not an alias edge, so it has no single target to name.

profiles.about: The profile inventory, tying three surfaces together. The NORMATIVE inventory is spec/conformance.md's own profile sections (ADR-0021 §3 clause 2), the implementation's is OL_CHECK_PROFILES, and this map is what makes them comparable. It is data rather than derived because the two spellings do not correspond mechanically -- `Interaction & Events` and `Tutor (AI)` do not become `interaction-events` and `tutor-ai` by any rule a reader could reconstruct -- so a guessed transformation would be a hand-maintained claim wearing an algorithm's clothes. Gated in BOTH directions: a profile added to spec/conformance.md with no checker id fails, and a checker id with no section fails.

profilesWithoutPrimitives.modules: The Modules profile's surface is the Core keywords `import` and `export` plus module resolution; it introduces no primitive of its own (spec/conformance.md's Modules section). ADR-0021 §5 additionally forbids a loaded library's procedures from ever entering this list -- they register through the ordinary phase-1 procedure table, so colliding with one raises ol-duplicate-definition, not ol-reserved-word.
profilesWithoutPrimitives.localization: Localization ships `alias` keyword packs -- alternate spellings declared in OpenLogo source -- rather than primitives (spec/conformance.md's Localization section). An alias spelling a program declares is a program name, not a built-in one.

tokenClassKeyword.about: spec/tooling.md's `keyword` TOKEN CLASS is a different set from the keyword list above, on purpose (spec/grammar.md:378), and it cannot be derived: measured against shipped output it OMITS some keywords (`and`/`or`/`not`/`mod`, which are `operator`), ADDS four words that are not built-in names at all (`empty`/`member`/`of`/`a`), and adds the profile words. Both a positional rule and "the keyword list minus the operators" were tried and refuted by measurement in issue #855.
tokenClassKeyword.rowFingerprintReason: A sha256 of the `keyword` row of spec/tooling.md's token-class table, byte for byte. It is a CHANGE DETECTOR and nothing more: it verifies the row has not changed, and verifies NOTHING about whether the row is correct. Stating that limit is the point. Issue #841 tried three stronger mechanisms across six review rounds -- hand-declared clause anchors (about twenty findings), then a fingerprint alone, then a fingerprint with derived claims layered on -- and every one of them overstated what it checked. The last and clearest: two clauses described as 'derived' were self-declared literals compared against the row, so they verified manifest-row AGREEMENT rather than truth, and inverting the sentence in both while recomputing the digest passed every check. The row is a long paragraph of English that spec/grammar.md:378 makes deliberately underivable; a mechanism claiming more than change detection over it has, repeatedly, been claiming something it did not check. What guards this row's CORRECTNESS is that spec/ is maintainer-owned under CODEOWNERS. What this digest guarantees is that a change to it cannot pass unseen -- silent drift becomes loud drift, which is the difference between the row shifting unnoticed and someone being made to look at it. The token-class enumeration therefore remains only partially guarded, and that gap is recorded on issue #841 rather than implied.

excluded.name: arc
excluded.rationale: Written in OpenLogo source (spec/geometry-module.md), so it is a library procedure rather than a primitive. A learner must stay free to build it from `repeat` and turns (spec/educational-model.md:169), and redefining a loaded one raises ol-duplicate-definition, never ol-reserved-word (spec/grammar.md:412).

excluded.name: a
excluded.rationale: Structural by position only (spec/grammar.md:380). `define a` is legal and `:p is a "point"` still reads as the predicate afterwards, because no declaration can occupy the position that makes the word structural.

excluded.name: empty
excluded.rationale: Structural by position only (spec/grammar.md:380). `define empty` is legal and `:x is empty` still reads as the predicate afterwards.

excluded.name: member
excluded.rationale: Structural by position only (spec/grammar.md:380). `define member` is legal and `2 is member of :nums` still reads as the predicate afterwards. Distinct from the Core reporter `member?`, which IS a built-in name.

excluded.name: of
excluded.rationale: Structural in two positions and a built-in name in neither (spec/grammar.md:380). `define of` is legal and `value of :d for key "a"` still reports the key's value afterwards. `positions` records where the grammar makes the word structural; it says nothing about how the word is painted, which is an independent axis (LDR-0007).
